CURRENT AUTHOR REVISION — Music System 2
For music work, read LOD-MUSIC-MS2-001 in 05, LOD-MUSIC-MS2-002 in 06 and LOD-MUSIC-MS2-TUNING in 07. MS2 replaces the older streamed-recording/media-cue music implementation and its no-live-synthesis restriction. Preserve the existing reactive MusicDirector gameplay, permission, floor, staging, victory and logging contracts. Historical MS1 paragraphs below remain historical where the new MS2 rules supersede them.

Fresh per-renderer/per-visit presentation entropy varies genuine returns without changing deterministic gameplay or floor assignment. Portable standard-MIDI exports retain all 1,402 curated clips with nine named instrument tracks plus conductor.

LOD-MUSIC-MS2 — ACTIVE MUSIC ROUTE
Local MIDI score, phrase catalog, mutators and musical identity → 05 LOD-MUSIC-MS2-001.
Player permission, renderer lifecycle, floor/block announcements and once-only victory → 06 LOD-MUSIC-MS2-002.
Exact synthesis, tempo/expression, clock/cache/voice budgets and validation limits → 07 LOD-MUSIC-MS2-TUNING.
MS2 supersedes MS1 recording streaming, remote origins, recorded-section import/playback and the prohibition on live synthesis. Existing reactive gameplay director rules continue unless explicitly replaced above.

Fresh per-renderer/per-visit presentation entropy varies genuine returns without changing deterministic gameplay or floor assignment. Portable standard-MIDI exports retain all 1,402 curated clips with nine named instrument tracks plus conductor.

LOD-MUSIC-MS2-001 — Music System 2 [AUTHOR-DIRECTED; SOURCE CANDIDATE; NATIVE ACCEPTANCE PENDING]
MS2 replaces MS1's streamed recording, section-cue, origin and media-cache design. The score uses the author's MIDI arrangements, curated offline into D-Dorian phrases and played locally by virtual instruments. One existing MusicDirector retains seeded, music-only floor assignment, frozen offered/active plans, staging/first-floor continuity, reversible spatial stair fades, pressure hysteresis, boss selection and accepted rescue/cash victory receipts. Wire roles T0/T1/T2/T3 mean authored Chill/Tension 2/Tension 3/Tension 4. BOSS and VICTORY remain special roles; INTERLUDE uses Chill. Block A supplies missing-role defaults.
Combat phrases retain rhythmic pulse; Chill selects quieter source phrases with sparse percussion. Two-bar phrases carry entering held notes, end gates at their boundary, and rank successors by cadence roots, shared pitch classes, energy continuity and source adjacency. The director varies gate, velocity, timing, timbre and occasional acid register without changing mode or gameplay RNG. Periodic fills preserve kick and melodic foundation. A shared musical grid, overlapping note releases and a quiet D bridge maintain continuity across phrases and transitions.
The countdown gradually raises BPM, at most six percent. Pitch and dynamics normally remain at baseline. Only confirmed recent combat with critical health, while playing Desperation or Boss, permits a subtle expression lift. Timer pressure alone, ordinary boss playback and staging do not raise pitch. Source compilation is an offline curation heuristic; native listening remains an acceptance gate.

LOD-MUSIC-MS2-002 — Local playback and lifecycle [AUTHOR-DIRECTED]
Server lod_music_enabled remains Off by default; saved player Music remains On by default, with saved volume. Either Off or zero music volume disposes the score renderer, note caches, native voices and pending music events. Gameplay effects and ambience retain their own controls. MS2 uses bundled MIDI event shards and a tiny synthetic tone/hit fallback bank; no music origin, HTTP audio requests, streamed PCM or client recording cache is required.
The client schedules local synthesis with a Web Audio renderer where supported and a finite Source-native voice pool otherwise. Both backends use the same composer, catalog and musical clock. Frame pressure reduces optional layers while preserving the score. A stalled scheduler discards expired attacks and resumes on the grid; it never replays note debt.
Existing private Die Logger block announcements remain tied to actual new block playback. Same-block role changes do not announce again. Victory remains once per accepted receipt; stale callbacks, reconnects, repeated snapshots and off/on toggles must not replay a fanfare. After its authored twelve-beat fanfare, AUTO continues the upcoming floor's Chill. Frozen catalog/plan revision mismatches produce a visible diagnostic rather than reinterpret an active plan.

LOD-MUSIC-MS2-TUNING — Implementation values [AUTHOR-DIRECTED; IMPLEMENTATION-TUNABLE]
Core source bank: eight blocks, 48 arrangements, 465 deduplicated MIDI stems. The current catalog contains 1,402 phrases and 170,860 orchestrated notes. Base tempo is the rounded median source tempo, currently 130 BPM; D Dorian is canonical. Clip time resolution is 48 ticks per quarter note, with melodic onsets curated to three ticks and drums to twelve ticks. Loop phrases are eight beats in 4/4; victory is twelve beats. Note payloads are split into Lua-returned JSON pages of at most 46,000 raw bytes.
Per-performance values: velocity 94–106%, gate 94–106%, timbre 90–110%, offbeat swing at most 0.3 tick plus onset humanization at most 0.175 tick. Acid may invert up one octave on a bar start with eight-percent probability within the instrument register. Recent-phrase exclusion retains three entries; each phrase stores six ranked successors. Fills occur every six to ten phrases of pulsed roles, replacing the final beat's snare/tom/hat attacks with a bounded roll. Bass and kick remain.
Tempo target: base × (1 + 0.06 × clamp(1 − authoritativeRemaining/1800, 0, 1)²), with maximum slew 0.3% of base per second. Remaining time comes from the existing effective campaign deadline, including Hourglass/Time Management. Expression: +22 cents and +8% note gain only with recent combat and HP at or below 20%, in T3/BOSS outside staging; otherwise zero lift.
Virtual instruments: mono resonant acid; gritty dual-oscillator industrial pad/rhythm guitar; detuned strings with calm/staging 180ms or combat 25ms attack; warm low-pass brass; mono bass with sub oscillator; two-voice tom; snare; kick; choking open/closed hats. Per-lane limits are 1/3/3/2/1/2/1/1/1; global note ceilings are 24 normally and 16 under frame pressure, plus one quiet D bridge per active/fading lane. Primary master processing uses 28Hz high-pass, 10.5kHz low-pass (8kHz reduced quality), and gentle 2.5:1 compression at −12dB.
Transport/cache bounds: at most two desired floor layers and two retired lanes, 1.2-second ordinary retired tails, 700ms equal-power gain fades, 650ms scheduling lookahead, 25ms scheduler tick, 2,048 queued events, eight note-page LRU entries and four arrangement LRU entries. The shared quarter-note grid plans twelve seconds ahead. A frame over 35ms selects reduced quality with five seconds of stable recovery. Native fallback uses one reusable generated identifier per instrument/hit, at most 1,024 pending attacks and 64 admissions per frame; expired attacks over 150ms late are discarded.
MS2's source gate and offline Chromium audio renderer check catalog integrity, mode, scheduling, one-shot fanfare, resource limits, audible instruments, unclipped output, musical continuity and Off. Garry's Mod native audio/Steam Deck/co-op acceptance remains separate. This rule supersedes MS1's media-download, folder-to-recording import, cue playback and no-live-synthesis restrictions; other gameplay authorities and release gates remain.
